solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Crazed legal expert dismissing judge as handy operator

parts.note: crazed means manic, wildly excited

indicators.note: the legal expert sends the judge away, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: a jurist is an expert in law

explanation.surface: A deranged lawyer sacks a judge, keeping company with someone good with their hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Handy operator' is playful: a manicurist literally works on hands.
explanation.definitionFit: A manicurist is a beautician who tends to clients' hands and nails, so is literally an operator on hands.

clue.text: Second volume ending in case for advocate

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A barrister wraps up a case in a moment with a second book.
explanation.definitionFit: To move a motion is to propose or recommend it, so move means put forward, advocate.

clue.text: Unusual ban on lover expressing love using hand gestures?

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary order, so the letters are rearranged
expressing means squeezing out, so the letter is pressed out of the pool

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: An odd ban on a lover declaring their love through sign language.
explanation.walkthrough: Squeeze one O (love) out of BANONLOVER and rearrange the remaining nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonverbal communication works without words, through gesture, expression and body language.

clue.text: Worked out fast, avoiding first chance after some thought?

parts.note: calculated means worked out by arithmetic

indicators.note: the first letter is avoided, so it is dropped

parts.note: brisk means fast

explanation.surface: Sums done quickly while skipping the first step are taken on spec.
explanation.definitionFit: A calculated risk is a gamble taken deliberately after weighing up the likely outcome.

clue.text: Airmen took flight offered by chance?

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force, Britain's airmen
fled means took flight, ran away

explanation.surface: Pilots ran away from an offer left to luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Something raffled is given as a prize in a lottery, so it is handed out by drawing tickets.

clue.text: Patron succeeded with little money, securing bridge team

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

indicators.note: securing means holding fast inside, so the team goes within

parts.note: poor means having little money
in bridge, North and South form one partnership

explanation.surface: A backer did well despite being short of cash, signing up a bridge pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor is a backer who funds an event or person, the same role as a patron.

clue.text: Present-day graduate rejected Bede?

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era of dates

indicators.note: rejected suggests thrown back, so the graduate's letters are read backwards

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: A modern graduate turns down the Venerable Bede, the medieval historian.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points to the Venerable Bede, the Anglo-Saxon monk; the definition is George Eliot's novel Adam Bede, whose hero's first name is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Bede is the title character of George Eliot's novel, so Bede is identified by the question mark as a surname example.

clue.text: I steered northwards, skirting hot Indian region

indicators.note: skirting means going round the edge, so the reversed letters surround the hot letter
in a down answer, going northwards means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: led means guided, steered
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A traveller heads north, bypassing a hot part of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi is a territory in northern India, containing the capital New Delhi.

clue.text: Educationalist provoking storm and noise

indicators.note: provoking means stirring up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A teacher stirring up a tempest and a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: Maria Montessori was the Italian educator whose child-centred method is used in Montessori schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Montessori was an Italian pioneer of early-childhood teaching methods.

clue.text: Be final: propose that location has area reduced by 50 per cent

parts.note: to bring up a topic is to propose it
there means that place

indicators.note: cut by half, so only the front half of the word area is kept

explanation.surface: Finish last: suggest the spot has its space cut in half.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up the rear is an idiom for coming last in a line or procession.

clue.text: Mostly nasty about US city recordings

indicators.note: about means around, so the shortened word goes round the city
mostly means not all of it, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: nasty means vile
NY is New York

explanation.surface: Most of what a big American city records is unpleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinyl is the plastic that gramophone records are pressed from, so it stands for records collectively.

clue.text: After surprise, I will abandon unfussy office layout

indicators.note: after means the next piece follows the first one in order

parts.note: to floor someone is to surprise or stun them

indicators.note: the letter I leaves, so it is removed from the word

parts.note: unfussy means plain

explanation.surface: Someone, after a shock, quits their fussy-free workplace arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A floor plan is a diagram showing how rooms and furniture are arranged on one storey.

clue.text: Getting quite drunk with ales ruins cocktail

indicators.note: drunk means mixed up and reeling, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Getting fairly tipsy on beers spoils a mixed drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A tequila sunrise is a mixed drink of tequila, orange juice and grenadine.

clue.text: Sculptor, Swiss at heart, came and got it wrong

indicators.note: got it wrong means the letters are put in the wrong order, rearranged
the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: An artist, Swiss deep down, turned up and misunderstood.
explanation.walkthrough: Alberto Giacometti really was a Swiss sculptor, known for his thin elongated figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Alberto Giacometti was a Swiss artist famous for tall, spindly bronze figures.

clue.text: Sort of motor — or band — I refitted

indicators.note: refitted means put together differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mechanic says he has refitted a kind of engine, or a band.
explanation.definitionFit: An inboard motor is a boat engine mounted inside the hull rather than on the stern.

clue.text: Harsh Republican political meeting ditching leader about nothing

indicators.note: about means around, so the shortened word wraps the zero
the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a caucus is a meeting of party members
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A rowdy Republican party gathering loses its chairman over nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Raucous describes a sound that is loud and grating, a synonym of a rough voice.

clue.text: Unaware first pair of lions occupies plain

indicators.note: occupies means sits inside, so the two letters go within

parts.note: plain means obvious
the first two letters of the word lions

explanation.surface: An oblivious creature as the leading lions take over the savanna.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblivious means not aware of what is happening around one.

clue.text: A hot-looking French lake recalled as product of volcanism

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: something that looks hot glows red
lac is French for lake

explanation.surface: A French lake that looks hot is remembered as the result of a volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: A caldera is formed when a volcano collapses, and often fills to make a crater lake, so the surface fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A caldera is a large crater formed when a volcano's summit collapses after an eruption.

clue.text: Rapid with notes, I'm accepted by a military association

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so the letters go inside the alliance

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance
taken as written, the letters of I'm without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone says they are welcomed swiftly into a military alliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Animato is a musical direction meaning lively, so it describes a brisk pace in music.

clue.text: King Edward possibly suppressing odd bits of talk and gossip

indicators.note: suppressing means holding down inside, so the letters go within the potato

parts.note: King Edward is a British potato variety, and tater is slang for potato

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first and third

explanation.surface: A king keeps a lid on stray snippets of chatter and rumour.
explanation.walkthrough: A King Edward is a popular British potato, so the king is a TATER, slang for potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattler is a person who chatters and spreads rumours, a gossip in the sense of the person.

clue.text: Nonsense about unknown work being source of material for play

indicators.note: about means around, so the nonsense wraps the unknown

parts.note: tosh is nonsense
algebra uses Y as an unknown
OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Rubbish about an unknown work being the basis for a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Play means children's play, not a drama on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A toyshop sells toys, the things children use when they play.

clue.text: Absence of work still involving some labour?

definitions.text: Absence of work still involving some labour?

parts.words: Absence of work still involving some labour
parts.note: time off a job that still includes labour in the sense of childbirth

explanation.walkthrough: Labour means childbirth here, not toil: the time off is given to new mothers.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the paid time off granted to an employee around giving birth, when labour is of the childbirth kind.

clue.text: Malicious blogger? Right to block impact

indicators.note: the letter blocks the word by sitting inside it

parts.note: toll means a damaging effect, impact, as in take its toll

explanation.surface: A spiteful blogger is right to prevent harm.
explanation.definitionFit: An internet troll posts deliberately provocative or abusive comments online.

clue.text: Printing ink: no source of colour used up

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means read upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: nay means no

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A printer's ink with no colour left, all used up.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyan is the greenish-blue process colour in four-colour printing, one of the standard inks.

clue.text: Philosophy briefly for every single European leader

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Taoism is a Chinese philosophy
each means every single one

explanation.surface: A short philosophy applied to every European head of government.
explanation.walkthrough: The Taoiseach is the prime minister of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The Taoiseach is the head of the Irish government, a leader of a European state.

clue.text: Completion of table leads to spare wood

indicators.note: leads to means the first piece comes ahead of the next
the completion of a word is its final letter

parts.note: spare means lean, thin, bony

explanation.surface: Finishing off a table leads to some leftover timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebony is a hard dark timber from tropical trees, used for furniture and piano keys.

clue.text: Island valley, not area offering no fruit?

indicators.note: not means leaving out, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a dale is a valley

explanation.surface: An island valley without farmland bears no crops.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle can mean futile or fruitless, as in idle threats, so it yields no result.

clue.text: Inducement to abandon English for French city, making measure of similarity

indicators.note: the English letter is given up and taken out of the word
for means in exchange for, so the city goes in where the letter left

parts.note: a come-on is an enticement or inducement
Paris is the French capital

explanation.surface: A bribe to leave England for Paris turns into weighing one thing against another.
explanation.definitionFit: A comparison is the act of weighing two things side by side to assess how alike they are.
